subsystems.name: Decoding pipeline
subsystems.role: converts recorded activity into a message.

subsystems.name: Encoding pipeline
subsystems.role: turns that message into stimulation parameters suited to the receiver's cortex.

subsystems.name: Transmission link
subsystems.role: carries the message between the two nervous systems, usually over ordinary digital networks.

subsystems.name: Neural stimulation
subsystems.role: writes the message into the receiver's brain.
parts: implanted electrode array with current drivers

subsystems.name: Timing and feedback
subsystems.role: keeps sender and receiver in step and lets them adapt.

subsystems.name: Safety and consent layer
subsystems.role: stops the interface harming or coercing a participant.

buildSteps.title: Map both brains
buildSteps.detail: Functional imaging and, where implanted electrodes exist, direct mapping locate the cortical areas that will be read from and written to.

buildSteps.title: Fit the sender's sensors
buildSteps.detail: An EEG cap is applied with conductive gel, or an already-implanted array is connected; signal quality is checked against a baseline.

buildSteps.title: Train the sender's decoder
buildSteps.detail: Over many sessions the sender performs a simple mental task, such as imagining a hand movement, while a classifier learns the pattern that distinguishes it.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the receiver's encoder
buildSteps.detail: Stimulation sites and intensities are tested until they reliably evoke a faint sensation — a phosphene, a twitch — that is noticeable but not painful.

buildSteps.title: Restrict to a low-bandwidth code
buildSteps.detail: Because the channel is so narrow, the pair agree on a simple code: one detectable signal means 'yes', its absence means 'no', and the task is built around that.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: The decoded state is transmitted, converted into a stimulus, and delivered to the receiver while both participants see the shared task and adjust.

buildSteps.title: Add error checking
buildSteps.detail: Redundant trials and confidence thresholds are used so that a single misread pattern does not become a wrong message.

buildSteps.title: Increase channel count
buildSteps.detail: More electrodes, sharper stimulation and better decoders are added step by step to raise the number of distinguishable signals.

prerequisites.why: implanted arrays lose signal over months, and scalp EEG is blurred by the skull.
classifiers already turn motor-imagery patterns into control signals for prostheses and spellers.

prerequisites.tech: Focal, non-invasive stimulation with millisecond precision
prerequisites.why: TMS is precise in time but coarse in space, so it excites broad patches of cortex rather than chosen neurons.

prerequisites.tech: A workable neural code for writing information
prerequisites.why: we can evoke crude sensations but cannot yet dictate what pattern of activity a specific perception requires.
the network side is easy; the bottleneck is entirely at the two brains.

pathway.milestone: laboratory demonstrations between a handful of participants, such as the University of Washington human-to-human link reported in 2014 and the three-person 'BrainNet' experiment published in 2019
pathway.unlocks: proof that a signal can pass from one nervous system into another, at a few bits per minute at best.

pathway.milestone: sensory-substitution and sensory-restoration research that reliably writes patterned activity into cortex
pathway.unlocks: a richer alphabet than a single on/off signal.

pathway.milestone: bidirectional closed-loop links in which both partners both send and receive, with learned mappings for each individual
a common neural interface standard with agreed codecs, consent rules and privacy protections
pathway.unlocks: any wider use — and forces society to decide what should never be shared between minds.
